title: VPN & Proxy Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to maximize your VPN and proxy privacy protection. Essential steps to secure your online anonymity and prevent data leaks.
intro: VPNs and proxies are powerful privacy tools, but they require proper configuration to truly protect your anonymity. This checklist ensures your connection is leak-proof, your provider is trustworthy, and your setup maximizes privacy protection against ISP tracking and surveillance.

items.task: Choose a no-logs VPN with proven track record
items.why: Many VPN providers claim no-logs policies but haven't been independently audited. Proven providers protect you even under legal pressure.
items.howTo: Research providers with third-party audits, court cases proving no-logs claims, and jurisdiction outside 5/9/14 Eyes countries. Avoid free VPNs that sell your data.

items.task: Enable VPN kill switch on all devices
items.why: Without a kill switch, your real IP address can leak if the VPN connection drops, exposing your identity and location to websites and ISPs.
items.howTo: In your VPN app settings, enable 'Kill Switch' or 'Network Lock'. Test by disconnecting VPN while browsing - internet should stop working until VPN reconnects.

items.why: DNS requests can reveal your browsing activity to your ISP even when using a VPN, completely bypassing your privacy protection.
items.howTo: Enable DNS leak protection in VPN settings. Use your VPN's DNS servers or configure secure DNS (1.1.1.1, 9.9.9.9). Test for leaks at dnsleaktest.com.

items.why: Different protocols offer varying levels of security, speed, and stealth. Some protocols are easier to block or detect by governments and ISPs.
items.howTo: Use WireGuard for best performance, OpenVPN for maximum compatibility, or stealth protocols if facing VPN blocking. Avoid PPTP and old protocols.

items.task: Test for IP and WebRTC leaks
items.why: WebRTC and other browser features can leak your real IP address even through VPNs, revealing your true location to websites.
items.howTo: Visit ipleak.net and browserleaks.com with VPN connected. Ensure only VPN IP shows, no local IPs. Disable WebRTC in browser or use Incognito Browser for automatic protection.

items.why: Public WiFi and untrusted networks can intercept your data. Auto-connect ensures you're always protected before any data is transmitted.
items.howTo: Configure VPN to auto-connect on startup and when joining new networks. Set trusted home networks as exceptions if desired for performance.

items.task: Disable IPv6 or ensure VPN IPv6 support
items.why: Many VPNs only route IPv4 traffic, leaving IPv6 requests exposed to your ISP and potentially revealing your real location.
items.howTo: Either choose a VPN with full IPv6 support or disable IPv6 on your devices. On Windows: Network settings > Adapter options > IPv6 unchecked.

items.why: Split tunneling can accidentally expose sensitive apps to your ISP while others use the VPN, creating privacy inconsistencies.
items.howTo: Disable split tunneling for maximum privacy, or carefully configure only non-sensitive apps to bypass VPN. Never exclude browsers or messaging apps.

items.task: Choose appropriate proxy type for your needs
items.why: Different proxy types offer varying privacy levels. HTTP proxies don't encrypt data, while SOCKS5 proxies provide better security and application support.
items.howTo: Use SOCKS5 proxies for better security and protocol support. Avoid HTTP proxies for sensitive browsing. Consider Tor for maximum anonymity when needed.

items.task: Configure proxy chains for enhanced anonymity
items.why: Single proxies can still track your activity. Chaining proxies through different providers and countries makes traffic analysis much more difficult.
items.howTo: Use tools like ProxyChains or configure multiple proxy layers. Ensure each proxy is from different providers and jurisdictions for maximum protection.

items.why: Weak or reused proxy credentials can be compromised, allowing others to use your proxy access and potentially monitor your traffic.
items.howTo: Use strong, unique passwords for proxy authentication. Store credentials securely and rotate them regularly. Enable 2FA where available.

items.why: Incorrect browser proxy configuration can leak DNS requests or bypass the proxy entirely for certain types of traffic.
items.howTo: Configure proxy in browser network settings or use browser extensions like FoxyProxy. Test configuration at whatismyipaddress.com. Consider using Incognito Browser with built-in proxy support.

items.why: Some applications may bypass system-wide VPN settings, sending data through your regular connection and exposing your activity.
items.howTo: Use VPN's app-specific routing features or proxy-aware applications. Monitor network connections to ensure all desired traffic routes through VPN/proxy.

items.task: Configure fallback protection for connection failures
items.why: When VPN or proxy connections fail, applications may automatically fall back to direct connections, exposing your real IP and data.
items.howTo: Enable strict firewall rules to block direct connections. Use applications that fail-closed rather than falling back to direct connections when proxy fails.
